tldr: To solve visual loss caused by dense smoke and geometric degeneracy in long straight tunnels in underground coal mines, we propose a robust odometry system that integrates 4D mmWave radar and wheel odometry alongside LiDAR, camera, and IMU, dynamically switching sensor constraints via online observability monitoring.
hero_caption: Comparison of mapping results across different methods in underground coal mine tunnels. While vision fails in smoke-filled Tunnel 1 and geometric degeneracy causes large drift in featureless Tunnel 3, only the proposed method (FIRE-Full) successfully and accurately navigates the entire course.
overview:
When operating autonomous mobile robots in extreme environments like underground coal mines or disaster sites, the biggest barrier is simultaneous sensor degeneracy. When visual degeneracy (complete visual loss due to fire and dust) and geometric degeneracy (point cloud slippage in long, featureless straight tunnels) strike at the same time, conventional SLAM methods that combine LiDAR, camera, and IMU diverge.

The authors brought in Doppler velocity from 4D mmWave radar (which can penetrate smoke and dust) and wheel odometry kinematic constraints (which do not depend on the external environment). Moreover, instead of just piling on sensors, they designed an online mechanism that computes a visual observability score based on an atmospheric scattering model and a geometric observability score based on Hessian eigenvalue analysis. By monitoring observation reliability, the system runs with standard LiDAR-visual-inertial fusion during normal conditions, boosts radar while dropping vision in smoke, and tightens wheel constraints in straight corridors—all dynamically switched within an iterated error-state Kalman filter (IESKF) framework.

In real-world experiments in underground coal mine tunnels, while baseline methods suffered from tracking loss in smoke or drift in long straight sections (drifts of tens of meters or crashes), the proposed FIRE-Full reliably finished the run with an average localization error of 5.677 m.
contributions: Built a tightly coupled odometry framework that integrates 4D mmWave radar point clouds and Doppler velocities, LiDAR, and sparse direct visual features within a unified VoxelMap, optimized via a single IESKF update step
Tightly coupled wheel odometry constraints incorporating non-holonomic constraints (NHC) and online lever-arm compensation to overcome geometric degeneracy in straight corridors

Proposed a degeneracy evasion strategy that evaluates visual observability online via an atmospheric scattering model (dark channel prior) and geometric observability via Hessian eigenvalue analysis, dynamically switching sensor fusion modes

Conducted real-world mobile robot experiments in harsh underground coal mine tunnels, demonstrating overwhelming robustness and high precision (average error of 5.677 m) under extreme conditions where conventional methods repeatedly failed

sections.heading: Extreme underground coal mines: Why do existing SLAM systems fail?
sections.summary: Underground coal mine roadways present a harsh environment where dense smoke and dust obscure vision while long, featureless straight structures cause geometric failure. Because existing LiDAR-camera-inertial systems break down when visual loss and geometric degeneracy occur simultaneously, this work proposes a new framework that adaptively combines 4D mmWave radar and wheel information.
sections.details:
High-accuracy, failure-immune SLAM is essential for underground coal mine roadway exploration and disaster rescue robotics. However, these environments present the worst possible combination of conditions for sensors: insufficient illumination, airborne dust, dense smoke, and featureless planar walls extending indefinitely.

The core challenge here is compound degeneracy:
- Visual degeneracy: Dense smoke strips away image contrast, destroying photometric consistency (the assumption that the same point shares the same brightness across views).
- Geometric degeneracy: In straight, featureless tunnels, LiDAR point cloud matching lacks constraints along the travel direction, causing the estimated pose to slip and drift.
- Inflexible fusion: Existing anti-degeneracy methods rely on fixed weighting or simple thresholding, failing to adapt when multiple degeneracies appear and alternate.

To address this challenge, the authors propose FIRE-LIVWO, which tightly couples the Doppler velocity of smoke-penetrating 4D mmWave radar and environment-independent wheel odometry within an iterated error-state Kalman filter (IESKF) framework, while detecting degenerate states in real time to switch fusion modes.

sections.heading: Related work: Multi-sensor fusion and the state of degeneracy detection
sections.summary: SLAM for harsh environments has evolved along two axes: ensuring redundancy through multi-sensor fusion, and degeneracy detection to decouple untrustworthy sensor data. This section reviews the lineage of LiDAR-visual-inertial fusion, the use of mmWave radar and wheel odometry, and the limitations of previous degeneracy countermeasures.
sections.details:
For localization in underground environments, LiDAR-Inertial Odometry (such as FAST-LIO2) that tightly couples LiDAR and IMU has served as a baseline. To compensate in geometrically featureless spaces, LiDAR-Visual-Inertial (LVI) systems (such as R3LIVE and FAST-LIVO2) adding cameras were developed, but they suffer from vision failing first under dense smoke.

Attention has therefore turned to 4D mmWave radar with its high dust penetration. Works such as 4DRadarSLAM, GaRLIO, and DR-LRIO increasingly leverage radar geometric features and Doppler velocity. Additionally, in tunnel driving, proprioceptive sensing via wheel encoders (wheel odometry) is extremely effective at suppressing longitudinal drift.

However, challenges have remained in degeneracy detection and adaptive fusion. While methods analyzing Hessian eigenvalues or using learning-based image enhancement exist, estimation diverges under prolonged sensor loss, and image enhancement fails completely in unlit darkness. This research aims to leverage the strengths of all these modalities, cleanly selecting between them according to their reliability.

sections.heading: Mathematical foundations: State definition and the error-state Kalman filter (IESKF)
sections.summary: We define the 18-dimensional state vector and the IESKF framework that iteratively optimizes sensor observation residuals. All residuals from LiDAR, radar, camera, and wheel odometry are formulated as a unified maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problem.
sections.details:
### State Definition and Sensor Synchronization
To estimate the robot's pose, the IMU frame is defined as the body frame, assuming time synchronization and rigid extrinsic calibration across all sensors (LiDAR, camera, IMU, wheel encoder, and 4D mmWave radar). The state vector to be estimated, $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{18}$, contains the IMU attitude, position, velocity, and gyro and accelerometer biases in the global frame.

### Iterative Update via IESKF
The system minimizes a cost function combining the prior distribution obtained from IMU propagation with the following residuals from each sensor (solved iteratively using Gauss-Newton, making it equivalent to an iterated Kalman filter):
- Radar Doppler velocity residual $\mathbf{r}_{R_V}$
- Radar geometric (point-to-plane) residual $\mathbf{r}_{R_G}$
- LiDAR geometric (point-to-plane) residual $\mathbf{r}_L$
- Camera photometric residual $\mathbf{r}_C$
- Wheel odometry velocity residual $\mathbf{r}_W$

In this way, all exteroceptive and proprioceptive observations are organized to be solved within a single unified optimization problem.

sections.heading: System overview: Architecture connecting three core modules
sections.summary: We present the overall architecture of FIRE-LIVWO, which performs simultaneous 6-DoF pose estimation and mapping. The system comprises three main modules: radar-enhanced LVI constraints, vehicle kinematics constraints, and degeneracy detection with adaptive mode switching.
sections.details:
FIRE-LIVWO's architecture is designed so that the differing strengths and weaknesses of various sensors in extreme environments complement each other seamlessly.

- (i) Radar-Enhanced LVI Constraint Module: Removes outliers from mmWave radar point clouds while generating Doppler velocity constraints. Furthermore, it registers both radar and LiDAR points into a shared octree-based "unified VoxelMap," building shared point-to-plane residuals and direct photometric residuals.
- (ii) Vehicle Kinematics Constraint Module: Synchronizes wheel encoder velocities to LiDAR timestamps, applying non-holonomic constraints (NHC) assuming zero lateral slip and online lever-arm compensation to correct translational velocity shifts during turns, constructing strong kinematic constraints.
- (iii) Degeneracy Detection & Adaptive Mode Switching Module: Computes a visual observability score $\mathcal{O}_V$ via an atmospheric scattering model and a geometric observability score $\mathcal{O}_G$ via geometric Hessian eigenvalue analysis in real time, dynamically toggling which residuals are active inside the IESKF.

sections.heading: Core technology details: Unified VoxelMap, kinematic constraints, and adaptive switching
sections.summary: We detail the design of geometric and photometric residuals seamlessly integrating LiDAR and radar, the formulation of wheel kinematic constraints, and the mechanics of the two degeneracy detection algorithms using an atmospheric scattering model and Hessian analysis.
sections.details:
### Unified VoxelMap and Feature Extraction
The authors adopted an adaptive octree VoxelMap with a root size of 0.5 m. Each leaf voxel maintains plane parameters and point collections. Cleverly, points derived from mmWave radar that lie on a plane are also adopted as visual map points alongside LiDAR points, associating an $8\times 8$ image patch. Thus, even if LiDAR points scatter in smoke, visual alignment can still be maintained using radar points.

### Formulation of Geometric, Doppler Velocity, and Photometric Residuals
- Geometric residuals: For each LiDAR and radar point, point-to-plane residuals against corresponding planes in the VoxelMap are constructed in a shared format.
- Doppler residuals: Using the radar's unique Doppler velocity measurements, the difference from the predicted line-of-sight velocity (derived from vehicle translational and angular velocities) is added as a constraint. This acts as an anchor preventing velocity and attitude divergence in dense smoke.
- Sparse direct photometric residuals: Map points are projected onto the current image, directly minimizing intensity errors against reference patches.

### Vehicle Kinematics Constraints
Translational velocity from wheel odometry is corrected for rotational effects $\lfloor\boldsymbol{\omega}\rfloor_\times$ due to the relative offset (lever arm) from the IMU. Then, a velocity residual $\mathbf{r}_W$ incorporating zero-lateral-slip non-holonomic constraints (NHC) in the body frame is formed. This keeps track of forward travel distance accurately even when external features disappear in straight tunnels.

### Degeneracy Detection and Adaptive Mode Switching
The system runs two independent detectors:
1. Visual degeneracy detection: Captures poor visibility in dense smoke using the classical atmospheric scattering model $I(\mathbf{u}) = J(\mathbf{u})t(\mathbf{u}) + A(1-t(\mathbf{u}))$. Using the Dark Channel Prior, transmission $\hat{t}(\mathbf{u})$ is estimated in real time, and its mean defines the visual observability score $\mathcal{O}_V$. When this drops below threshold $\mathcal{O}_V^{th}$ ($\mathcal{D}_V=1$), visual residuals are disabled (or down-weighted), bringing radar Doppler constraints to the forefront.
2. Geometric degeneracy detection: Extracts the pose sub-block from the geometric Hessian matrix $\mathbf{H}_G$ of point-to-plane ICP and performs eigenvalue decomposition. The geometric observability score $\mathcal{O}_G$ is computed from the ratio of maximum to minimum eigenvalues. When the eigenvalue in a specific direction (such as along the tunnel axis) drops severely past a threshold ($\mathcal{D}_G=1$), the system switches modes to boost wheel odometry constraints.

This achieves fully autonomous switching across standard "LIV mode", smoke-filled "LIVR mode", geometrically degenerate "LIVW mode", and the worst-case "LIVRW mode" where both occur at once.

sections.heading: Empirical validation: Testing performance in coal mine smoke and long tunnels
sections.summary: Using a Husky A200 robot, evaluation was conducted in actual coal mine roadways containing both smoke-filled sections and featureless straight sections. While other methods diverged or dropped out one after another, the proposed FIRE-Full completed the course with an outstanding average error of 5.677 m, confirming that adaptive switching functioned as intended.
sections.details:
### Experimental Environment and Setup
Validation was conducted across a route connecting three tunnels in an actual underground coal mine (see Fig. F3):
- Tunnel 1: Textured, but filled with high-density smoke and dust (visual degeneracy area).
- Tunnel 2: Clear of smoke, but relatively feature-sparse.
- Tunnel 3: Clear of smoke, but an extreme geometric degeneracy area where identical cross-sections continue indefinitely.

The robot (Husky A200) was equipped with a Livox AVIA LiDAR, Hikvision camera, Oculii Eagle 4D mmWave radar, and wheel encoders, all hardware-synchronized. Ground truth was established using 20 total station coordinate points, compared via average localization error (AvgErr).

### Trajectory Accuracy and Mapping Comparison
The results were striking (Fig. F4, Fig. F5, Table II):
- FAST-LIVO2 and FIRE-LIVW, which rely on vision and LiDAR, immediately diverged and crashed upon entering the smoke of Tunnel 1 due to visual mismatch.
- Radar-less FIRE-Base and R3LIVE managed to pass the smoke but slipped in Tunnel 3's geometric degeneracy, producing large errors of 23.962 m and 31.596 m, respectively.
- Radar SLAM (4DRadarSLAM) did not crash in smoke, but due to point cloud sparsity, drifted upwards along the Z-axis by over 15 m, reaching an AvgErr of 45.453 m. GaRLIO also could not withstand Tunnel 3's geometric degeneracy, leaving a 17.212 m error.
- In contrast, the full configuration of the proposed method (FIRE-Full) breached the smoke using radar, constrained the straight tunnel using wheel odometry, and finished the run with an average error of just 5.677 m.

### Degeneracy Detection and Adaptive Switching Behavior
The detectors' operation is clearly corroborated by the data:
- Geometric score $\mathcal{O}_G$ (Fig. F6): Remained around 35 in textured Tunnel 1, but spiked upon entering Tunnel 3, peaking at 114.2. The eigenvector corresponding to the minimum eigenvalue aligned precisely with the tunnel axis, prompting the system to immediately activate wheel constraints (LIVW mode) to prevent drift.
- Visual score $\mathcal{O}_V$ (Fig. F7): From 0.88 at the entrance of Tunnel 1, the score plummeted to 0.02 in the deepest smoke ($x=25$ m). The system disabled vision and switched to radar-dominant LIVR mode, resuming visual tracking at $x=53$ m (score 0.66) once clear of the smoke.

captions.F5: Time-series estimated trajectories (X and Z axes) across methods. While FAST-LIVO2 and others diverge in the smoke area (a1), and many methods drift substantially along the X-axis in the geometrically degenerate area (a2), only FIRE-Full (blue line) closely tracks the total station ground-truth points (red stars).
captions.F6: Evolution of geometric observability score $\mathcal{O}_G$ and visualization of Hessian eigenvectors. Upon entering featureless Tunnel 3, the score surges past the red threshold (40) to reach 114.2, detecting the complete loss of constraints along the travel direction and triggering wheel constraints.
captions.F7: Variation of visual observability score $\mathcal{O}_V$ and onboard camera views in the smoke section. As smoke thickens, the transmission score plunges to 0.02; once below the threshold (0.4), visual residuals are decoupled to transition to radar dominance, resuming visual tracking after exiting the smoke.

sections.heading: Conclusion: A pathway to odometry immune to environmental degeneracy
sections.summary: We summarize the achievements of FIRE-LIVWO, which integrates the penetrative capability of 4D mmWave radar and geometric wheel constraints via IESKF, realizing dynamic switching based on observability analysis. It substantially boosts long-distance autonomous navigation robustness in extreme underground environments.
sections.details:
This paper presented "FIRE-LIVWO", an odometry system tailored for extreme environments like underground coal mines where dense smoke/dust and geometric degeneracy strike at the same time.

By combining multimodal geometric and photometric modeling in a unified VoxelMap, 4D mmWave radar Doppler velocity constraints, and NHC-aware wheel odometry constraints, the system achieves a level of redundancy unattainable by single-sensor setups. Furthermore, its greatest strength lies in not merely blending sensors, but using an atmospheric scattering model and Hessian analysis to assess in real time "which sensor is currently failing" and switch modes intelligently.

Thorough comparative experiments in a real-world environment proved that it consistently delivers low error (5.677 m) even under punishing scenarios where conventional methods fail completely. The code has been open-sourced on GitHub to benefit the community.

takeaways: In extreme-environment SLAM, it is essential not merely to stack sensors, but to quantify which sensor is becoming unreliable using physical models (scattering models and Hessian analysis) and decouple them dynamically.

4D mmWave radar Doppler velocity constraints provide an extraordinarily strong safeguard against velocity and attitude divergence when LiDAR and camera geometric or photometric alignments fail completely in dense smoke.

In long, self-similar environments like straight tunnels where exteroceptive sensors fundamentally degenerate, properly calibrating and tightly coupling proprioceptive sensing like wheel odometry (motion measurement independent of the outside world) is decisive.
limitations: Visual degeneracy detection via atmospheric scattering models (Dark Channel Prior) works well in smoke and fog, but its discriminatory ability in completely unlit pitch-black settings or under extreme lighting fluctuations requires further validation.
Wheel odometry constraints can become an error source in muddy terrain with heavy slipping or when driving over rubble, as wheel slip detection and decoupling are not yet addressed.
Because mmWave radar point clouds are sparse and noisy on their own, maintaining high-accuracy 3D mapping with radar alone when LiDAR fails entirely remains difficult.
